summary: Digital identity verifiers run and assure identity proofing for banks, fintechs, governments and platforms. They review flagged document and selfie checks, tune liveness and deepfake defenses, verify mobile driver's licenses and EU Digital Identity Wallet credentials, and prove compliance with NIST SP 800-63-4, eIDAS 2.0 and KYC/AML rules. AI helps most with triaging review queues, mapping controls to standards, analyzing fraud patterns, and writing clear policies and notices to users. Decisions about real people stay with the human reviewer.

prompts.title: Manual review case triage
prompts.task: Structure a decision on an identity check that the automated pipeline flagged
prompts.prompt: You are a senior identity proofing analyst. An automated verification for [USE CASE, e.g. bank account opening] was flagged. Vendor signals: document check [RESULT/SCORES], liveness/PAD [RESULT], face match [SCORE AND THRESHOLD], device/IP signals [DETAILS], data source checks [RESULTS]. Target assurance level: [e.g. NIST 800-63-4 IAL2]. I have removed personal data. Give me: (1) a table of each signal, what it suggests, and how much weight it deserves; (2) benign explanations versus fraud explanations; (3) extra evidence or step-up checks I could request, such as an NFC chip read or a supervised remote session; (4) an approve, step-up, or decline recommendation and your confidence in it. Do not treat a face match score alone as proof.
prompts.caution: Never paste raw ID images, biometrics or full personal data into the chat. The human reviewer makes and owns the decision, and adverse-action and appeal rules still apply.

prompts.title: Assurance level gap analysis
prompts.task: Map an identity proofing flow to NIST SP 800-63-4 and eIDAS levels
prompts.prompt: Act as an identity assurance consultant. Our onboarding flow: [STEP-BY-STEP DESCRIPTION, including evidence collected, validation method, verification method, and remote, supervised or in-person]. We need to meet [NIST SP 800-63A-4 IAL1/2/3 and/or eIDAS LoA substantial/high, ETSI TS 119 461, UK DIATF]. Produce a gap table with these columns: requirement (cite the section), current control, status (met/partial/missing), and suggested fix. Then list the top 3 risks from the gaps. Say which requirements you are unsure of or that changed between 800-63-3 and revision 4, so that I check them against the official text.
prompts.caution: Standard section numbers and wording must be checked against the published documents before an audit.

prompts.title: Deepfake and injection attack spike analysis
prompts.task: Investigate a rise in suspected synthetic-face or camera-injection attacks
prompts.prompt: You are a fraud analytics lead for a remote identity verification service. Over [TIME PERIOD], our liveness failures rose from [X%] to [Y%]. These summary stats were exported from [TOOL/VENDOR DASHBOARD]: [PASTE AGGREGATE DATA: device types, OS, virtual camera flags, emulator flags, geography, time of day, document types]. Help me (1) form hypotheses that separate presentation attacks, digital injection/virtual camera attacks, and benign causes such as a bad app release; (2) propose queries or cuts of the data to test each one; (3) suggest defensive controls, referring to ISO/IEC 30107-3 PAD testing and CEN/TS 18099 injection-attack guidance where relevant. Keep everything defensive: no instructions on how to create attacks.
prompts.caution: Use aggregated or pseudonymized data only. Do not ask for or use details on how to make deepfakes.

prompts.title: mDL and wallet verifier integration plan
prompts.task: Plan acceptance of mobile driver's licenses and EUDI Wallet credentials
prompts.prompt: Act as a digital credentials architect. We want to accept [ISO/IEC 18013-5 mDL in person / ISO/IEC 18013-7 or OpenID4VP online / EU Digital Identity Wallet PID] for [USE CASE] in [JURISDICTIONS]. Our stack: [SYSTEMS]. Produce a phased plan covering: issuer trust lists (e.g. AAMVA DTS, EU trusted lists), selective disclosure and data minimization (request only [ATTRIBUTES NEEDED]), relying-party registration, fallback for users without a wallet, logging, and test plans. End with a list of open questions, marking any whose specs or regulations are still changing.
prompts.caution: Wallet specs and eIDAS implementing acts are still changing. Confirm current versions before you build.

prompts.title: Plain-language verification notice
prompts.task: Explain biometric verification, data use and recourse to end users
prompts.prompt: You are a UX writer who specializes in privacy. Draft the screen text and a short FAQ for users who are asked to verify their identity with [ID DOCUMENT + SELFIE / mDL / WALLET] on [PRODUCT]. Facts: data collected [LIST], purpose [PURPOSE], retention [PERIOD], processor [VENDOR], legal basis [e.g. consent / legal obligation], alternative methods offered [LIST], how to appeal a failed check [PROCESS]. Write at an 8th-grade reading level and keep it under 200 words for the screen. Note which items probably need specific consent wording under [GDPR Art. 9 / Illinois BIPA / other], and mark them for legal review.
prompts.caution: This is draft wording only. Counsel must approve the consent language, especially for biometric laws.

prompts.title: Bias and accessibility audit plan
prompts.task: Design a test of verification outcomes across demographic and accessibility groups
prompts.prompt: Act as an algorithmic fairness auditor. Our identity verification pipeline uses [VENDOR/MODELS] for document authentication, liveness and face matching. Design an audit plan that measures false rejection and false acceptance rates across [GROUPS, e.g. age, skin tone, document type, disability, older devices]. Include: metrics and statistical tests, sample size reasoning, how to get representative data lawfully, references to NIST FRTE/FATE demographic results and to the 800-63-4 performance requirements, accessibility issues (e.g. users with visual or motor impairments), and how to report the results to [STAKEHOLDERS]. Point out where collecting demographic data itself raises privacy risks.
prompts.caution: Collecting demographic or biometric data for testing needs its own legal basis and a DPIA.

prompts.title: Incident report for an identity breach
prompts.task: Document a verification bypass or credential fraud incident
prompts.prompt: You are an incident response writer for an identity verification team. Draft a post-incident report from these notes: [TIMELINE, DETECTION METHOD, NUMBER OF ACCOUNTS AFFECTED, ATTACK VECTOR AT A HIGH LEVEL, CONTAINMENT STEPS, VENDOR INVOLVEMENT]. Sections: executive summary, impact, root cause, contributing factors, remediation with owners and dates, detection improvements, and notification obligations to check (e.g. GDPR 72-hour breach notice, state breach laws, SAR/FinCEN filing if [REGULATED ENTITY]). Write it blameless and factual, and list any facts still unknown.
prompts.caution: Legal and compliance decide which notifications and filings are required. Keep exploit details at a high level.

prompts.title: Upskilling roadmap
prompts.task: Build a learning plan for the evolving field of digital identity
prompts.prompt: I am a [CURRENT ROLE, e.g. KYC analyst / fraud investigator / IAM engineer] moving into digital identity verification and credential assurance. I have [HOURS/WEEK] for [MONTHS]. Build a week-by-week plan covering: NIST SP 800-63-4, eIDAS 2.0 and the EUDI Wallet, W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0, OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP, ISO/IEC 18013-5/-7, FIDO2/passkeys, presentation attack detection (ISO/IEC 30107), and KYC/AML basics (FATF guidance on digital ID). For each topic, give the primary source to read, a hands-on exercise, and a self-check question. Name relevant certifications only if you are confident they exist, and tell me to confirm their current details.
